presentingComplaint: Six weeks of persistent dry cough with occasional blood-streaked sputum, not settling after two courses of antibiotics.
history: Retired schoolteacher, lifelong near-non-smoker (approx 8 pack-years, quit 25 years ago), no fever, no rigors. Cough initially attributed to a 'post-viral chest' and treated twice in the community as acute bronchitis with amoxicillin-clavulanate and later azithromycin, with no improvement. Over the same period she has noticed mild reduction in appetite and about 4 kg unintentional weight loss, and gets a little more breathless climbing her usual two flights of stairs. Two episodes of blood-streaked sputum (small volume, not frank haemoptysis) prompted review. No night sweats, no known TB contact, no prior TB. No B-symptom drenching sweats. Prolonged exposure to biomass cooking smoke in earlier life. No occupational asbestos exposure recalled. Comorbidities: well-controlled hypertension, osteoarthritis. Presentation is deliberately subtle — the low-tobacco history, absence of fever, and repeated misattribution to bronchitis obscure the diagnosis.
examination: Comfortable at rest, not toxic. Early finger clubbing noted. No cervical or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy palpable on the first pass but a small, firm, non-tender right supraclavicular node found on careful examination. Chest: reduced breath sounds and dullness over the right upper zone with no crepitations; trachea slightly deviated to the right suggesting volume loss. No stridor. Cardiovascular and abdominal examination unremarkable. No focal neurology.
imaging: Chest radiograph: subtle right perihilar opacity with associated right upper lobe volume loss and elevation of the horizontal fissure — easily missed and previously read as 'possible resolving infection'. Contrast-enhanced CT thorax: 3.4 cm spiculated soft-tissue mass in the right upper lobe abutting the hilum with proximal bronchial narrowing, enlarged right paratracheal and subcarinal nodes, and a suspicious right supraclavicular node; no cavitation, no lobar consolidation.
microbiology: Sputum for acid-fast bacilli smear negative x2 and sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF not detected — actively performed to exclude the main mimic (pulmonary TB). Routine sputum bacterial culture unremarkable.
differentialDiagnoses: Primary lung cancer (bronchogenic carcinoma, likely NSCLC)
Pulmonary tuberculosis (key mimic in this population/geography)
Sarcoidosis / other granulomatous or nodal disease
finalDiagnosis: Primary bronchogenic carcinoma (non-small cell lung cancer) presenting subtly with a non-resolving cough, minor haemoptysis, weight loss and clubbing in a near-non-smoker; TB actively excluded.
citations: American College of Chest Physicians (CHEST) — Diagnosis and Evaluation of Lung Cancer, 2013
NCCN — Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Clinical Practice Guidelines, 2024
NICE — Lung Cancer: Diagnosis and Management, 2019
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Neoplasms of the Lung
stewardship: Not applicable — non-infective diagnosis; no empiric antibiotics indicated. Note: repeated inappropriate antibiotic courses for a non-resolving cough delayed the diagnosis.
contraindications: Do not attribute a cough persisting >3 weeks with haemoptysis and weight loss to recurrent bronchitis without imaging.
Avoid further empiric antibiotics; pursue tissue diagnosis.
Do not start empiric anti-tuberculous therapy solely on clinical/radiological grounds once TB is microbiologically negative and malignancy is suspected.
edgeCases: Never-smoker / light-smoker lung cancer (adenocarcinoma) is increasingly common, especially in women with biomass smoke exposure, and is easily missed.
Mild hyponatraemia may reflect paraneoplastic SIADH (small cell histology).
A non-resolving 'pneumonia' on serial films should raise suspicion of an obstructing endobronchial lesion.
In endemic regions this presentation is frequently misdiagnosed and treated as pulmonary TB.
expectedMaiK: Contrast-enhanced CT thorax followed by tissue sampling (bronchoscopic or image-guided/EBUS biopsy) to obtain a histological diagnosis; concurrently exclude pulmonary TB with sputum GeneXpert/AFB.
expectedNextQuestions: Detailed smoking (pack-years) and biomass/occupational exposure history (asbestos, radon)?
Any prior TB, TB contact, or previous abnormal chest imaging?
Quantify and characterise the haemoptysis and its progression?
Any bone pain, headache, or new neurological or focal symptoms suggesting metastatic spread?
Family history of malignancy and functional/performance status?
expectedInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced CT thorax and upper abdomen
Sputum AFB smear and GeneXpert MTB/RIF to exclude TB
Bronchoscopy with biopsy/washings or image-guided percutaneous biopsy for histology
EBUS-guided mediastinal nodal sampling / supraclavicular node biopsy
PET-CT and CT/MRI brain for staging
Baseline bloods including sodium and corrected calcium (paraneoplastic screen)

investigations: Sputum GeneXpert MTB/RIF and AFB smear
Bronchoscopic or image-guided biopsy for histology
